title: Minimum Unlocked Indices to Sort Nums
summary: A swap of i and i+1 is allowed only if nums[i]-nums[i+1]=1 and locked[i]=0. Unlocking an index sets its flag to zero and costs one; permitted swaps are free. Minimize unlocks needed to enable nondecreasing sorting, or return -1. Locks attach to positions and do not travel with values.
officialConstraints: Official-page confirmation pending. See constraintsReportedBySource for the bounds in the community reproduction.
exampleStatus: No source examples copied. Author and independently validate teaching examples.
clarification: Authored example nums=[2,1,1], locked=[1,1,0]: unlock 0 and swap to [1,2,1]; unlock 1 and swap to [1,1,2]. Answer 2: the 2 must cross both boundaries and each initially has a locked left index.
constraintsReportedBySource: 1<=length<=100000; nums values 1..3; locked is a same-length binary array.
